title: observability: add token-level KV cache metrics, refined dashboards, and alert tuning
author: Aisha Khan
description:
Motivation: Production customers asked for finer-grained visibility into per-token cost and latency breakdowns and KV cache behavior during high-concurrency workloads. This PR adds token-level KV cache metrics, integrates tracing hooks for cache operations, ships a curated Grafana dashboard for token-level cost/latency/KV insights, and adjusts alert thresholds to reduce noise while preserving SLO protection.

What changed: Implemented new Prometheus metrics (token_kv_cache_hits_total, token_kv_cache_misses_total, token_kv_cache_hit_latency_seconds_bucket, token_token_cost_tokens_total) and corresponding labels (model, deployment, route, customer_id, cache_region). Added tracing spans around KV cache read/write and cache-warm paths. Created a token-level Grafana dashboard with pre-built panels for cost-per-token, latency distribution by token position, KV hit rate heatmaps, and tail latency percentiles. Tuned existing SLO alerts: lowered firing thresholds for end-to-end P99 latency when KV hit rate drops below 85%, added an aggregate alert for token-cost regressions, and converted several noisy alerts from page to ticket.

Backward compatibility and rollout: Metrics are additive and exported under the observability namespace. Dashboard is added with a feature flag (observability.token_kv_dashboard_enabled). Rollout plan: staged deploy to canary -> beta -> all regions over 3 days, with alert suppressions enabled during canary stabilization.

Testing and performance: Added unit tests for metric labels and integration tests to validate tracing spans are emitted. Ran load perf canary against a synthetic chat workload (seq_len=512) and observed ~1% overhead in CPU metrics and no measurable latency regression.

Notes: Documentation and README updated with metric names, dashboard import JSON, and runbook for the new alerts. Related Linear issues: ENG-4123 (token observability), SRE-88 (alert tuning). Support ticket SUP-2147 requested KV hit visibility for a customer rollback investigation.
commits: Add token-level KV cache metrics and labels (aisha/metrics/token_kv_metrics.go)
Add tracing spans and tests for KV cache operations (aisha/tracing/token_kv_tracing.go + tests)
Dashboard JSON + alert tuning and docs (observability/dashboards/token_kv_dashboard.json, docs/observability/token_metrics.md)
review_comments: Liam: Nice surface area. Please ensure label cardinality is bounded — can we avoid customer_id for high-volume metrics?
Aisha: Good point — switched customer_id to a low-cardinality id_hash and added sampling in high-throughput paths (see registry.go).
Maya: Alert tuning looks reasonable, but add a suppression window for the first 12h after rollout to avoid noisy pages.
Aisha: Added suppression and will annotate alerts with rollout metadata. Also added runbook steps for escalation.
Zoe: Tracing spans look good; please add an example trace in the docs. Aisha: Done in token_metrics.md (example trace section).
merge_outcome: Merged after 2 approvals; CI green and perf canary passed. Alerts suppressed during rollout window.
release_notes: Added token-level KV cache metrics and Grafana dashboard; tuned alerts to reduce false positives. New metrics: token_kv_cache_hits_total, token_kv_cache_misses_total, token_kv_cache_hit_latency_seconds_bucket, token_token_cost_tokens_total. Dashboard available behind feature flag observability.token_kv_dashboard_enabled.
